claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of 10.21 g/cm³.
HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Additively manufacturing HfMoTaTiZr as a lattice or cellular structure will reduce its overall density.
A lattice architecture can reduce material in non-critical load paths while concentrating load-bearing in optimized struts.
Cell size, strut thickness, and node geometry are the architectural variables used to control the HfMoTaTiZr lattice.
The BCC structure of HfMoTaTiZr has inherently high stiffness.
The stiffness of the BCC structure will allow lattice struts to carry load similarly to as-cast bulk HfMoTaTiZr.
Load-bearing reinforcement will be maintained despite reducing the overall amount of material.
The additively manufactured specimens will have an overall density below approximately 10 g/cm³.
The additively manufactured specimens will achieve approximately a 12% density reduction relative to the 10.21 g/cm³ baseline.
The lattice specimens will retain at least 90% of the baseline room-temperature yield strength, corresponding to approximately 1440 MPa.
The lattice specimens will retain at least 90% of the baseline yield strength at 1000 °C, corresponding to approximately 770 MPa.
The hypothesis is bounded to compressive loading from ambient temperature through 1000 °C.
Stress concentrations at lattice nodes may adversely affect ductility or fatigue performance.

contradictions.description: A 12% reduction from 10.21 g/cm³ corresponds to about 8.98 g/cm³, whereas the predicted outcome describes density below approximately 10 g/cm³ as approximately a 12% reduction. Merely reaching just below 10 g/cm³ would represent only about a 2% reduction and would fail the stated 12% rejection threshold.
